text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian government adopts Serbian Justice Ministry report rejecting as unfounded allegations of irregularities in local elections in eight municipalities as cited in the OSCE report.
- Serbian government prepares for spring sowing and draws up plans for providing fertiliser and diesel fuel to farmers.
- Yugoslavia and France start social security cooperation talks in Paris.
- Yugoslav government submits to the federal parliament agreement with Croatia on suspension of visas for official and diplomatic passport holders.
- New round of former Yugoslavia succession talks starts in Brussels. Yugoslav delegation headed by Kosta Mihajlovic.
- Zastava car factory plans to complete 1,500 cars on its assembly lines by end of January.
- Yugoslav average wage in December was 881 dinars, or 11.9 percent up in nominal terms and seven percent in real terms on the previous month, says federal statistics office.
- Yugoslav, Serbian and Montenegrin governments at joint meeting conclude money supply has not gone up in January. Current situation in monetary and foreign exchange sectors still complex.
- Industrial output rose 7.1 percent in 1996 against 1995, says statistics office.
- Problems in Kosovo province can only be resolved within the scope of Serbia and Yugoslavia, Albanians and Serbs must live together, says Yugoslav interior minister Vukasin Jokanovic.
- Another murder in Belgrade brings to nine the total toll in the capital in nine days and will make January 1997 one of the "bloodiest" in the capital's crime chronicles.
NASA BORBA
- Police cordons in central Belgrade remain in place before protesting students, joined by lawyers, university professors and citizens. Students vow to stay "as long as it takes."
- Leader of National Front of France Jean-Marie Le Pen on visit to Belgrade expresses sympathy for Belgrade students protesting against the annulment of local election results.
- Farmers vow not to enter any contracts on spring sowing before they are paid for the sunflower, sugar beet and soybean from last year's harvest.
BORBA
- Federal government concludes at its meeting with republican governments that Yugoslavia should seek status of developing country within the World Trade Organisation.

- Yugoslav textile industry sees way out of difficulties in unified imports of raw materials for which $17 million are needed, said official of the Yugoslav chamber of economy textile committee Vera Paranos.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Secret terrorist organisation "Liberation Army of Kosova" claims responsibility for car bomb attack on Pristina university rector.

- Deans of 16 Belgrade University faculties and directors of five research institutes appeal to Serbian Interior Ministry to withdraw police cordons blocking student protesters. -- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 4305
